Your Skin Barrier: Ceramides, Hydration and Over-Exfoliation

Signs your barrier is struggling, and a calm, step-by-step approach to helping it recover.

By GlowHer Editorial Team · 29 September 2026

Educational content only, not medical advice. Some pages may contain affiliate links. Read our disclosure.

In this article

  1. Signs the barrier is struggling
  2. Common causes
  3. A calm reset
  4. When to get help

The outermost layer of the skin works like a brick wall. Skin cells are the bricks, and lipids such as ceramides, cholesterol and fatty acids act as the mortar. When it is healthy, skin holds water and resists irritants.

Signs the barrier is struggling

  • Stinging when you apply products that used to feel fine
  • Tightness, flaking or rough patches
  • Redness or a shiny, tight look
  • Sudden breakouts alongside dryness

Common causes

Over-exfoliating, stacking many actives, harsh cleansers, very hot water and cold, dry weather can all contribute.

A calm reset

  1. Pause exfoliating acids, retinoids and scrubs.
  2. Switch to a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser.
  3. Use a ceramide-rich moisturizer morning and evening.
  4. Keep up with sunscreen every morning.
  5. Reintroduce actives slowly once skin feels comfortable again.

When to get help

If irritation lasts more than a couple of weeks, spreads or is painful, see a doctor or dermatologist. It may be a skin condition that needs a different approach.
